constraint: Only ordinary Quest type/counter consumers/producers. Quest intrinsic actors remain separately exact-rule-boundary evidence; no category-wide exclusion applies to these eleven cards.

subrules.rule: Each Quest card has a striated text box containing a number of quest symbols. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.
An quest symbol is a keyword ability that represents a triggered ability referred to as an quest ability.

subrules.name: 744.2a
subrules.rule: An quest symbol includes a number, indicated here as “{N}.”

subrules.name: 744.2b
subrules.rule: “{N}—[Effect]” means “When one or more quest counters are put onto this Quest, if the number of quest counters on it was less than N and became at least N, [effect].”

subrules.name: 744.2d
subrules.rule: An Quest’s final quest number is the greatest value among quest abilities. If an Quest somehow has no quest abilities, its final quest number is 0.
Quests use quest counters to track their progress.

subrules.name: 744.3a
subrules.rule: As an Quest enters the battlefield, its controller puts a quest counter on it.

subrules.name: 744.3b
subrules.rule: Each Quest has a triggered ability that “adds a quest counter.” To add a quest counter, put a quest counter on the Quest that is the source of that triggered ability.

If the number of quest counters on an Quest permanent is greater than or equal to its final quest number, and it isn't the source of a quest ability that has triggered but not yet left the stack, that Quest's controller sacrifices it. This state-based action doesn't use the stack.
